english.title: Tachograph - cause improper function / use
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), caused **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) to use a vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), to which section 97 of the Transport Act 1968 applied when the recording equipment installed in the said vehicle in accordance with the Community Recording Equipment Regulation

(A)_[did not comply with the relevant Annexes to that Regulation, (as to tachograph functionality)]_
(B)_[was not used as provided by Articles 13 to 15 of that Regulation]_

in that **(..SPECIFY CONTRAVENTION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 97(1)(a) of the Transport Act 1968.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
caused the use of a vehicle
to which section 97 Transport Act 1968 applied
when recording equipment installed in the vehicle
in accordance with Community Recording Equipment Regulation
did not comply with the relevant Annexes to that regulation OR
was not used as provided by Articles 13 to 15 of that Regulation

english.notes:
(i) Option A - functionality - refers to for example, breakage of seals, lack of calibration and defects within the tachograph . Option B - covers the improper use of the tachograph and may be used where the driver has failed to enter information onto the face of the tachograph record sheet.
(ii) Where the place of offence is uncertain, see section 103(7) of the Act, which provides that an offence may be treated as having been committed at the place of driving, the person's place of residence or the principal place of business.
(iii) Section 97(7) defines the "Community Recording Equipment Regulation" as Council Regulation (EEC ) No. 3821/85, as amended.
(iv) Each breach may be charged separately if this is appropriate to the facts of the case.
(v) Statement of Facts procedure applies - see end of document for wording.
(vi) Further detail may be included in the **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) option in addition to the identity of the driver, e.g. the defendant's capacity ("caused Mr. Peter Jones, who was employed by him as a driver ").
(vi) See also offence wordings: H3158 and H3160.

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
